purpose: Preserve exact/event authority while maintaining an immutable versioned resident semantic graph plus bounded event-driven latent activation that can shape the next Assembly before an LLM explicitly requests memory retrieval.

layers.role: versioned witnesses/pointers into authoritative exact/event stores
immutable resident typed semantic/provenance index for a validated source-corpus revision
immutable additions/removals/status changes relative to a base epoch; atomically published after validation
event/cue-driven sparse salience field with lazy decay, local propagation, inhibition and bounded active set; evolves between LLM calls
select exact/FTS/packet/local-graph/multihop route and decide whether latent activation is sufficient, supplemental or ignored
freeze a bounded model-visible organ from pinned graph epoch + activation epoch + CognitiveFrame and required exact anchors
explain route, epochs, activation ancestry, semantic paths, conflicts, evidence families, exact witnesses and cost

epoch_contract.publish_rule: authoritative event/state commit first -> semantic delta preparation -> provenance/status/integrity validation -> immutable epoch publish -> activation may reference/preadapt to published epoch
epoch_contract.reader_rule: a query/Assembly pins one graph_epoch_id; mixed old/new semantic views are invalid
epoch_contract.reclamation_rule: old epochs remain readable until no pinned reader/Assembly requires them; concrete RCU/MVCC implementation is an implementation choice, not semantic authority
epoch_contract.failure_rule: failed/unknown delta validation does not publish; previous epoch remains current and direct authoritative fallback stays available

delta_compaction_policy.principle: incremental maintenance is conditional, not universal
delta_compaction_policy.decision: keep delta overlay while amortized update savings exceed query+memory+integrity costs; otherwise build a new immutable base epoch
delta_compaction_policy.proxy_observation: In the Cycle-4 30k-node lexical proxy, 10% changed nodes favored overlay at publish time but rebuild amortized after ~974 queries; at 20% changed nodes full rebuild was already cheaper than overlay construction. Not a production threshold.

rules: activation changes salience only, never epistemic status
default propagation is local/bounded and may be zero-hop for exact cues
decay is timestamp/lazy where possible rather than O(N) global sweep
negative/conflict/revoked facts retain status even when active
activation cannot create a semantic edge or capability
active set has hard node/energy/time budgets
feedback from model outcome can change future salience only through typed receipts

epoching.basis_frame_id: optional until Assembly, required for current-state model visibility

assembly_contract.rule: Assembly membership is temporary and distinct from graph persistence and activation salience. Current/exact claims require exact-anchor validation even if highly active.

reader_projection.rule: canonical graph form and small-model projection are separate; explicit relation roles preferred until target reader proves compact equivalence
reader_projection.context_budget: Assembly exposes only bounded selected state; latent field itself is not dumped into prompt

frank_mapping.M.MEMORY_FABRIC: owns semantic epochs, latent activation and Assembly compilation
frank_mapping.M.COGNITIVE_FRAME_ASSEMBLER: provides frame witness pinned into current-state Assembly
frank_mapping.M.WORKSPACE_ARBITER: receives Assembly candidates; workspace competition/ignition remains distinct from memory activation

hard_invariants: one Assembly cannot mix graph epochs
shared ancestry is not independent evidence
no secrets/bearer capabilities in model-visible graph

evidence_boundary.historical_recovery: supports mechanism continuity, not new empirical confidence
evidence_boundary.cycle4_delta_proxy: supports adaptive overlay/rebuild policy in synthetic Python structures
evidence_boundary.cycle4_latent_proxy: supports feasibility of sparse lazy field updates in synthetic graph
evidence_boundary.external: current literature independently studies spreading activation, incremental memory and bitemporal graph memory
